subject: Next steps: deployment mode & PoC success criteria — Acme Health
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Tom Park <tom.park@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 14:05:00 -0400
Subject: Post-call recap and proposed PoC activities

Hi Lena / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and a proposed lightweight PoC plan so we can lock down the right deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) for Acme Health. High level: you indicated production latency needs (~<250ms p50 on short prompts), strict PHI handling for a subset of workflows, and desire for predictable monthly spend for billing team.

Proposed next steps (short):
- We run a 3-week PoC focused on the most sensitive workflow (patient intake summarization) using a RedWood-hosted model first to validate function and latency.
- Parallel security review: Marissa will collect the SOC2 and network docs for your security team.
- Week 2: If latency and data controls need it, we can spin a Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) for a 1-week burst test or stand up a Private VPC eval on your staging VPC.

Please find an initial PoC checklist attached (acme_poc_checklist.xlsx) and a hosting comparison PDF (redwood_hosting_comparison.pdf). Ive also included a draft success-criteria table in the Drive link I shared.

Can you confirm: 1) decision maker for deployment mode (is Procurement the final approver?) 2) preferred start week (we suggested May 17) 3) any pre-approved compliance docs we should send now?

Thanks — happy to hop back on a short call to triage.

—Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: acme_poc_checklist.xlsx, redwood_hosting_comparison.pdf
From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Park <tom.park@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap and proposed PoC activities

Hi Sean —

Appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers:
- Final approval for deployment mode will land with Procurement (cc'd) and our Security lead (internal) — Procurement will need the cost delta figures for Dedicated and Private.
- May 17 start works for our engineering team (well block calendar).
- Please send SOC2 + data handling process documents; our security reviewer will need them to pre-approve the Hosted path.

Two asks from our side before we start the PoC:
1) A short checklist of what network access (IPs/VPN/VPC peering) is required for the Private VPC option so we can scope network approvals.
2) A simple cost template showing the incremental monthly committed cost for Dedicated (per-100k tokens baseline) so Procurement can review.

If you can send both by EOD Tuesday, Ill get Procurement and Security to review ahead of May 17.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz
Director, AI Initiatives | Acme Health
lena.ortiz@acmehealth.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Tom Park <tom.park@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 10:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap and proposed PoC activities

Lena —

Acknowledged. Ive pulled together the two items and attached a short network checklist and a Dedicated cost sketch (see redwood_hosting_comparison.pdf for the high-level). Key notes:
- Private VPC: typical packet from customers is either VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink. Minimal firewall rules we need are outbound to our control-plane endpoints and (optional) ingress rules for SSH/management. Ive summarized required ports/IPs in the attached checklist.
- Dedicated cost sketch: we show committed monthly pool pricing and a burst/overage line item tied to GPU hours; the attached PDF has a simple per-100k tokens example.

Marissa — can you drop the SOC2 summary and the link to the full security pack into this thread so Procurement/Security have what they need? Karthik, if youre available mid-week, can you be on call for the PoC kick on the 17th to support infra setup?

Thanks — Sean

On Tue, May 11, 2027 at 10:12 AM, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmehealth.com> wrote:

>
> L

Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 08:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap and proposed PoC activities

Hi all —

Attaching the SOC2 summary and the security pack link (redwood SOC2 attestation and network diagrams). For Procurement, the short answers:
- Hosted: standard SOC2 + encryption at rest/in-transit; suitable for de-identified PHI workflows.
- Dedicated: same controls with tenant isolation and SLA options (uptime and latency SLOs).
- Private VPC: customers control network; we provide KMS integrations and audit log export.

Lena — I added a one-page SLA excerpt to the Drive link and put the SOC2 PDF in the shared folder. If you want, we can push a short redlineable MS Word SLA for Procurement to review next week.

Marissa Cole
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf
From: Tom Park <tom.park@acmehealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 09:30:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-call recap and proposed PoC activities

Thanks everyone — Procurement confirmed theyll review the cost sketch and SLA excerpt by Friday. A couple clarifications from Engineering (cc'd by Lena during stand-up):
- For the PoC, we want to run two parallel arms: hosted (to validate functionality) and a 48-hour Dedicated burst test for latency-sensitive samples. Can Redwood support log export for the 48-hour burst (wed like access to per-request latency traces)?
- If Dedicated looks good, Procurement will need an MSA + pricing appendix; early signal is favorable.

If Redwood can confirm the burst Dedicated plan and the trace export capability, were green to start May 17.

-Tom
